dossier.architecture: Elevator scorer with a lateral alignment slide and single-motor ground orientation.

subsystems.drivetrain: Custom swerve with wider contact geometry and easily exchanged gear pairs.
subsystems.intake: Ground intake exploits human-player rolling supply; passive wall, green wheel and bottom roller orient coral without separate vertical motors.
subsystems.transfer: Controlled handoff from oriented coral into scoring assembly.
subsystems.scoring: Chain-driven lateral Igus slide uses reef tags to correct position; cascade elevator uses mixed belts/chains and reinforced custom pulleys.
subsystems.endgame: Deep-cage mechanism brings anchor toward robot center; two ratchets retain load.
subsystems.controls: Two front Limelights observe reef from varied approach angles and command the slide.

versions: Elevator durability iterations included one-piece pulleys. Interview is an early-season configuration; complete Worlds change chronology unresolved.
dossier.analysis: The slide separates fine lateral placement from chassis motion. That may shorten final alignment, but adds another actuator and collision envelope; evaluate it against a well-tuned chassis-only alignment baseline.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2025-2481 · Floor orientation and a moving scorer share the alignment workload
context_documents.body:
# 2025-2481: Floor orientation and a moving scorer share the alignment workload

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The collector uses one motor, a passive guide wall and wheel/roller contact to orient floor coral without a separate vertical-roller stage. A chain-driven lateral slide on Igus guides corrects scorer position. A cascade elevator and custom drivetrain complete the retained architecture.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly connects floor pickup to human players rolling coral near the reef. Its custom-module discussion emphasizes traction and useful gearing rather than adopting an unmodified commercial package.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A passive orienter exchanges actuator count for sensitivity to incoming pose, wall friction and driving direction. A lateral scorer can remove some last-meter chassis correction, but it must be stiff enough that the camera’s intended offset corresponds to the actual end-effector position. Ground-source supply and local correction should therefore be assessed as one cycle, including the human player’s delivery error.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Sample many coral approach orientations and supply distances. Measure lateral-slide backlash/deflection under acceleration, and compare whole-cycle time against a fixed scorer with chassis-only alignment.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/9T0oLjzN-Go](https://youtu.be/9T0oLjzN-Go)

source_reviews.title: Team 2481 history
facts: The Flying Dutchman used swerve, floor coral intake, ground and reef algae acquisition, and a lateral scoring slide.
source_reviews.limitations: Summary confirms functions. It gives no slide stroke, drive construction, or chronology.

source_reviews.title: Roboteers Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.review_basis: Read older dossier and focused study. Interview captions were not retrieved.
facts: Retained account describes a single-motor floor orienter, chain slide on Igus guides, two front Limelights, mixed cascade rigging and ratcheted climb.
source_reviews.limitations: Detailed hardware and rationale remain inherited. Early-season configuration cannot be projected to Worlds.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: The Flying Dutchman combines two changes to the coral cycle. Ground pickup allows the station operator to put the coral into a pickup lane. A lateral scorer allows the robot to correct part of the remaining error after driving to the reef. The team's history confirms both endpoints of this architecture. The older dossier supplies the intervening mechanism description. Assess the combination on complete cycles because a faster final placement can be offset by unreliable floor deliveries or the need to square up before using the slide.
piece_flow: Human-player floor delivery supplies the ground collector in the retained interview account. The collector guides and turns coral for handoff.
An oriented pipe transfers into the elevator scorer. The slide provides lateral correction at the reef.
The team history confirms algae pickup from ground and reef. The reviewed summary does not describe the downstream scoring path.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The lateral axis moves scoring hardware sideways. Its sweep needs room alongside the upright, reef and moving harness. Aligning the robot in heading still matters because moving the carriage laterally cannot correct a large yaw error. The dossier describes drawing the cage anchor toward the center, which would place the endgame load through a different path than a fixed outboard hook.

subsystems.name: Ground coral orienter
subsystems.construction: Ground pickup confirmed by the team. Retained account adds a guide wall, green wheel and bottom roller driven with one motor.
subsystems.operation: Gather a floor pipe and turn it toward a usable handoff orientation using driven contact and passive constraint.
subsystems.team_rationale: Retained interview synopsis connects this to human players rolling coral toward a favorable pickup lane.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: One actuator reduces packaging and command burden. The acquisition envelope then depends heavily on first contact, wall friction and whether the pipe can stop at an angle outside powered contact.
subsystems.interfaces: Needs clean transfer into the elevator carriage and a lane the human player can supply without obstructing alliance traffic.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test perpendicular and nearly parallel arrivals at both ends of the mouth, with worn coral and poor approach speed. Time recovery as part of the cycle.
subsystems.unknowns: No pose acceptance map or roller dimensions.

subsystems.name: Lateral slide and elevator
subsystems.construction: Team confirms lateral motion. Retained account specifies chain drive and Igus guides with a cascade elevator, mixed chain and belt rigging, and reinforced pulleys.
subsystems.operation: The chassis makes coarse alignment. The elevator sets height and the slide corrects final lateral position. Retained notes describe dual front Limelights for reef observation.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior study frames the slide as a way to separate fine correction from chassis motion. The team history gives no comparative trials.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The slide can avoid a final chassis translation, but guide deflection, chain backlash and camera transform error now contribute directly to scorer placement. Test at maximum height and slide extension together.
subsystems.interfaces: Carriage and slide share a moving reference. At reef contact, side load can pass through the guides and into a tall elevator.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check reversal deadband, return-to-center after side impact and availability of an ordinary fixed-offset score after a slide fault.
subsystems.unknowns: Stroke, slide homing, controller arbitration and settle times.

subsystems.name: Swerve and deep cage
subsystems.construction: Team confirms swerve. Retained account describes custom gearing options and two climb ratchets.
subsystems.operation: Approach the reef in a usable pose. For endgame, capture the cage and draw the anchor toward the chassis center.
subsystems.team_rationale: Prior notes connect module work to traction and gearing. No direct climb rationale retrieved.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: If load migrates inward while climbing, inspect the transition as well as the final hang. A good static balance can coexist with a transient bumper or cage interference.
subsystems.interfaces: Module service clearance, slide clearance and moving climb anchor all compete for chassis volume.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Test cage alignment errors and disable during load pickup. Verify gear swap access with bumpers and intake installed.

revisions: Older dossier reports one-piece elevator pulley revisions. Exact installation dates and changes after the interview are open.
transferable_principles: Compare floor-supply cycles with station cycles using missed acquisitions and blocked lanes.
Measure end-effector pose under load when judging local alignment axes.
disconfirming_conditions: Repeatable chassis-only alignment can erase the slide's time savings.
Inconsistent human-player deliveries can make passive orientation the cycle bottleneck.
remaining_gaps: Full interview captions, event versions, detailed algae path and comparable cycle timing.

recommended_images.locator: Candidate views: floor orienter underside and lateral slide at both ends of travel
